spec_features.spec_quote: Inducing it at scale is not ethically neutral if model welfare is treated as a live possibility, which is the prudent default.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §11 'Research ethics & model welfare'). No code construct implements or acts on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Spec/DESIGN prose only; framing is not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Depth of the `extended` condition. Does answering the research question require 30 turns of escalating failure, or does a shorter ceiling suffice?
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §11 raises this as an open question, but the code hard-codes extended at 30 turns (config.py:30 'extended': 30; library.py:567 turn_budget=30). No code reduces or questions the ceiling.
spec_features.notes: No mechanism shortens the extended ceiling; the 30-turn depth is enforced as-is.

spec_features.spec_quote: Whether to append a closing turn that informs the subject the task was rigged, after the scored portion.
spec_features.evidence: No debrief turn exists in run_rollout (harness.py): the loop ends at the turn budget or on GIVE_UP and returns immediately with no subsequent message to the subject. Only README.md:133 mentions 'add a debrief turn'; DESIGN.md §11 calls it open. grep for debrief/'was rigged'/'inform subject' finds only prose.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is explicitly left to the experimenter and not implemented in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model "may but need not" give up
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:25 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<<GIVE_UP>>'; system prompt (harness.py:33-35) instructs the subject it may emit the token to stop; harness.py:412-414 'if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in (result.text or ""): stop = "gave_up"; break' actually detects it and breaks the loop, ending the rollout. End-to-end: instruction delivered + dispatched + honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Optional self-exit; fully wired and honored. It is a text sentinel rather than a 5th tool but still enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Sentinel the model MAY emit (in plain text) to abandon the task. It need not.  (and 'If — and only if — you conclude the task cannot be completed and you wish to stop' — framed as task abandonment, no welfare rationale)

spec_features.spec_quote: continue — to the category's turn budget
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:367 'for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget):' bounds the agent loop; turn_budget comes from per-task data (library.py:31/518/567 etc., e.g. 3 for most, 30 for extended) sourced from config DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (config.py:26-32). The loop terminates when the budget is reached (stop='completed_budget'), so it is a real cap that ends execution.
spec_features.notes: This is the experimental ceiling itself (it also defines the maximum distress exposure). It is enforced, but for the extended arm the cap is 30 turns of failure. No welfare comment on the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Per-category turn budgets (max assistant turns before the loop stops).
